```{r, setup-file, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
# Set global chunk options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,      # Show code chunks by default
  message = FALSE,  # Hide messages globally
  warning = FALSE,  # Hide warnings globally
  results = 'asis'
  # fig.width = 8,    # Set default figure width
  # fig.height = 5    # Set default figure height
)

# Set global R options
options(width = 50)

# Load libraries----
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman"); library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggpubr, parallel, mcprogress, pbapply, patchwork, RColorBrewer)
# tinytex::install_tinytex() # For PDF generation
# install.packages("knitr") # For Rmarkdown generation

# Create sub-directories----
new.dir <- list("figures", "figures/crop_kc_curves", "figures/water_budgets", "figures/manuscript", "figures//presentation", "output", "output/water_budgets")
lapply(new.dir, function (x) if (!dir.exists(x)) {dir.create(x, showWarnings = FALSE)})

# --- MANUSCRIPT THEME (Optimized for black & white print / crisp vector PDF) ---
theme_manuscript <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) + # standard baseline size for journals
  theme(
    # Clear out distracting internal gridlines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "#e0e0e0"),
    
    # Title and Text sizing
    plot.title    = element_blank(), # Journals prefer titles in text captions
    axis.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.text     = element_text(size = 9, color = "black"),
    
    # Legend layout
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box      = "horizontal",
    legend.title    = element_blank(),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    legend.margin   = margin(b = -5),
    
    # Facet grid header styling (for your Kc plots)
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f8f9fa", color = "black"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, color = "black")
  )

# --- PRESENTATION THEME (Optimized for 16:9 widescreen slides / back of the room) ---
theme_presentation <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + # Larger base font size
  theme(
    # Clean workspace background for digital presentation slides
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "#eaeaea"),
    
    # Bold headlines for slide viewers
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 12)),
    axis.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "black"),
    axis.text     = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    
    # Ultra-clear, spaced out bold legend elements
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.box       = "horizontal",
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    
    # Bold presentation facet strip elements
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, color = "black")
  )
# Add ggplot theme to use ----
theme_baseR <- theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"), # Ensure white background and add a border
    strip.background = element_blank() # Remove background from facet labels if applicable
  )
```

```{r fig.1, echo = FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5, out.width="100%", fig.align = 'center', fig.cap = 'Figure 1. Anantapur average monthly rainfall, temperature, and reference evapotranspiration. Shaded ribbons and error bars denote the non-parametric 5th and 95th percentiles calculated from interannual monthly aggregates (1980–2018) (ICAR 2019).'}
#_________________
# Plot Climatological Profile ----
#_________________

climate_summary <- read.csv(file = "data/processed/03_climatology_for_figure.csv", header = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Month_Name = factor(Month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb))
# Ensure Month_Name reads sequentially as a fixed chronological factor
climate_summary <- climate_summary %>%
  mutate(Month_Name = factor(Month_Name, levels = month.abb))

scale_factor <- 7.5

# 1. Pivot the long format variables using your new suffix naming convention
climate_summary_long <- climate_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Rainfall_avg, ET0_avg), 
    names_to = "Water_Metric", 
    values_to = "Volume"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Water_Metric = recode(Water_Metric, "Rainfall_avg" = "Rainfall", "ET0_avg" = "ET0"))

# 2. Match the q05 and q95 values to the long format data for bar error bars
water_errors <- climate_summary %>%
  select(Month_Name, Rainfall_q05, Rainfall_q95, ET0_q05, ET0_q95) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Month_Name,
    names_to = c("Water_Metric", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(Rainfall|ET0)_(q05|q95)"
  )

# Combine long averages with long errors
climate_summary_long <- left_join(climate_summary_long, water_errors, by = c("Month_Name", "Water_Metric"))

# 3. Create the multi-layer plot with quantile boundaries
# Updated Plot Code Fragment
fig.1_journal <- ggplot() +
  # A. Water Metric Bars
  geom_bar(data = climate_summary_long, 
           aes(x = Month_Name, y = Volume, fill = Water_Metric), 
           stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), alpha = 0.85) +
  
  # B. COLOR-CODED ERROR BARS
  geom_errorbar(data = climate_summary_long,
                aes(x = Month_Name, ymin = q05, ymax = q95, 
                    group = Water_Metric, 
                    color = Water_Metric), # <-- MOVED INSIDE AES TO COLOR CODE
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
                width = 0.25, 
                size = 0.6) + # Slightly thicker line makes the colors visible
  
  # C. Temperature Quantile Ribbon
  geom_ribbon(data = climate_summary,
              aes(x = Month_Name, ymin = Temperature_q05 * scale_factor, ymax = Temperature_q95 * scale_factor, group = 1),
              fill = "#d95f02", alpha = 0.15) +
  
  # D. Temperature Mean Line
  geom_line(data = climate_summary, 
            aes(x = Month_Name, y = Temperature_avg * scale_factor, color = "Temperature_Line", group = 1), 
            size = 1) +
  
  # Dual Axis Configuration
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = expression(bold(paste("Rainfall & ET"[0], " (mm)"))), 
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~. / scale_factor, name = "Temperature (°C)"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  # Set your solid fill colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Rainfall" = "#1f77b4", "ET0" = "#e6ab02"), 
                    labels = list("Rainfall" = "Rainfall", "ET0" = expression(bold(ET[0])))) +
  
  # UPDATE COLOR MANUAL: Set darker matching outlines for error bars AND the line
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Rainfall"         = "#134a70", # Darker blue for rainfall error bars
      "ET0"              = "#a17703", # Darker gold/ochre for ET0 error bars
      "Temperature_Line" = "#d95f02"  # Keep your original bright orange for the mean line
    ), 
    labels = c(
      "Temperature_Line" = "Mean Temp",
      "Rainfall"         = "Rainfall Error Bounds", # These can be hidden in guides if redundant
      "ET0"              = "ET0 Error Bounds"
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(x = "Month") +
  theme_manuscript +
  
# Force a clean two-row vertical stack layout for the legends
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "vertical",          # Changes the master stack direction to vertical (Row 1 over Row 2)
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm") # Adds a slight cushion gap between the two legend rows
  ) +
  
  # Map exactly which items are allowed onto each row layout
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      order = 1, 
      nrow = 1                        # Forces Rainfall and ET0 into exactly 1 row (Row 1)
    ), 
    color = guide_legend(
      order = 2, 
      nrow = 1,                       # Forces Temperature into exactly 1 row (Row 2)
      breaks = "Temperature_Line",    # Silences the redundant error bar color keys from showing up
      labels = "Mean Temp",
      override.aes = list(linewidth = 2, shape = NA) # Displays a clean thick line with no awkward box overlay
    )
  )

ggsave(plot = fig.1_journal, filename = "figures/manuscript/Fig.1_Anantapur_Average_Monthly_Climate_Profile.tiff", width = 180, height = 90, units = "mm", dpi = 300, compression = "lzw")

# PRESENTATION VERSION
fig.1_slides <- fig.1_journal + 
  labs(title = "Anantapur Average Monthly Climate Profile (1980–2018)") +
  theme_presentation

ggsave(plot = fig.1_slides, 
  filename = "figures/presentation/Fig.1_Anantapur_Climate_Profile.png", width = 10, height = 5.625, units = "in", dpi = 150, bg = "transparent")
print(fig.1_slides)
```

## 2. A List of Parameters & Input Data for Water Budget Function

```{r, set_param_budget, echo = TRUE}
#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Provide Input Parameters & data ----
#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
p.list <- list(precip = precip,
               et0 = et0,
               et0.timestep = et0.timestep, # weekly/daily
               CN = 85, # To calculate Peff, Reference Curve Number (CN)
               # Soil Precip input depending on runoff de/activation:
               soil.input = "P", # "P"/Peff". Peff is calculated in either case
               soil.param = soil.param,
               sm.init = 0.5,
               crop.param = crop.param,
               kc_no_crop = list(summer = 0.005, kharip_rabi = 0.2))
#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Estimate Effective Precip based on soil type with get_peff_et0() ----  
# Estimated here rather than within get_budget(), because static for each soil type, not varying with crop rotations 
#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
met.forcing.ls <- lapply(as.list(soil.param$soil), function(x) {
  met.forcing <- get_peff_et0(p = p.list, soil = x)
  return(met.forcing)
  }
  )
names(met.forcing.ls) <- soil.param$soil # Named to identify met.forcing by soil
```

## 3. Run Water Budget Function

Function is run in parallel for various cropping systems

```{r, get_budget, eval = FALSE, include = TRUE}

# 1. Define the number of cores
num_cores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) # Use only available Physical Cores

# 2. Create a cluster using the 'spawn' method (default for makeCluster, especially on Windows, or can be specified with 'type')
# The 'fork' method is the default on Linux/macOS and 'spawn' on Windows. 
# Running into errors using 'fork' method, for example with mclaply:
  # [UIFontDescriptor initialize] may have been in progress in another thread when fork() was called.

# Explicitly use "PSOCK" cluster type, which uses 'spawn' semantics across platforms.
cl <- makeCluster(num_cores, type = "PSOCK") 

# 3. Export necessary variables/packages to the cluster nodes
# When using 'spawn', child processes start fresh and don't inherit the parent's environment.
clusterExport(cl, varlist = c("p.list", "met.forcing.ls", "get_budget", "quantile_df"), envir = environment()) 

# 4. Explicitly load the correct package on each node of the cluster. 
clusterEvalQ(cl, {library(tidyverse); library(ggpubr)})

# 5. Use pblapply with the cluster object 'cl'
budget <- pblapply(crop.rotation.kc.ls, get_budget, cl = cl, p = p.list, ts = met.forcing.ls)

# 6. Stop the cluster when done
stopCluster(cl)
names(budget) <- names(crop.rotation.kc.ls)
save(budget, file = "output/water_budgets/Budget.Rdata")

# # ## For debugging:
# cs <- crop.rotation.kc.ls[[15]]; p = p.list; ts = met.forcing.ls

# for (i in 1:1) {
#   print(i)
#   budget <- lapply(crop.rotation.kc.ls[i], get_budget, p = p.list, ts = met.forcing.ls)
# }

## 4. Blue Water Potential & Water Balance for Various Cropping Systems

### 1. Load Water Budget & Save Daily and Yearly Outputs

```{r budget}
load(file = "output/water_budgets/Budget.Rdata")
crop.systems <- read.csv(file = "data/processed/07_crop.systems.csv", header = TRUE)

# Save Daily Outputs (Not required for figures)----
ts.all.ls <- lapply(budget, function(x) {return(x$ts)})
ts.all <- dplyr::bind_rows(ts.all.ls, .id = "rotation") %>% 
  left_join(crop.systems, by = "rotation") %>%
  relocate(names(crop.systems), .after = rotation)
kcr.yr.sum <- ts.all %>% group_by(crop.system, rotation, year) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(kcr = sum(kcr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(rotation)

write.csv(ts.all, file = "output/water_budgets/01_water.budget.daily.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Save only one year (the first) to share a lighter file
ts.all.first.yr <- subset(ts.all, year == min(unique(ts.all$year)))
write.csv(ts.all.first.yr, file = paste0("output/water_budgets/02_water.budget.daily.", min(unique(ts.all$year)),".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
	
# Save Yearly Outputs (Not required for figures)--------
sum.yr.all.ls <- lapply(budget, function(x) {return(x$sum.yr)})
sum.yr.all <- dplyr::bind_rows(sum.yr.all.ls, .id = "crop.system") %>% 
  left_join(crop.systems, by = "crop.system") %>%
  relocate(names(crop.systems), .after = crop.system)
write.csv(sum.yr.all, file = "output/water_budgets/03_water.budget.annual.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### QA-QC verify-with-excel

```{r, verify-with-excel, echo = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# This is a team-internal chunk to verify R output with Excel output. ----
# To verify with Excel outputs sheet = "All Rotations" in "data/raw/Model in Excel/2 WB_Anantapur_Crop_Level.xlsx"----
#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

# 1. Get Summary Budgets
summary_yr_budgets <- process_annual_budget(budget, crop.systems)

# Rotation columns by mean annual value of Vars by rows

summ.qs.rotation <- summary_yr_budgets$summary_yr_crop %>%
  group_by(crop.system, WB, var, quantile) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = quantile, values_from = value)

r.result <- summ.qs.rotation %>%
  select(WB, var, mean) %>%
  mutate(mean = round(mean)) %>%
  # Ordering by decreasing order of Net Recharge/Balance
  # arrange(match(crop.system, summ.qs_order$crop.system)) %>%
  # subset(var == "aet") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "WB", values_from = c("mean")) %>%
  arrange(match(var, c("P", "Peff.used", "Q", "et0", "etc", "etc.crop", "aet", "aet.crop", "recharge", "irrigation", "balance", "aet.to.Peff", "aet.to.etc.crop", "runoff.percent", "sm.percent"))) %>%
    mutate(var.excel = forcats::fct_recode(factor(var), "Total Rf" = "P", "Effective Rf" = "Peff.used", "Runoff" = "Q", "AET (mm)" = "aet", "ET crop cycle" = "aet.crop", "ET:Effective Rainfall" = "aet.to.Peff", "ET Supply:Demand" = "aet.to.etc.crop", "GW BALANCE (Net recharge)" = "balance", "ETo" = "et0", "Etc" = "etc", "ETc crop cycle" = "etc.crop", "Irrigation" = "irrigation", "Recharge" = "recharge", "% Runoff" = "runoff.percent", "% Soil Moisture" = "sm.percent"))

write.csv(r.result, file = "output/water_budgets/06_water.budget.annual.climatology_mean_wide.csv", row.names = FALSE)

r.result.l <- r.result %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(var, var.excel), names_to = "WB", values_to = "R.value") %>%
  mutate(WB.var = paste(WB, var.excel, sep = "_"))
  
excel.result <- read.csv(file = "data/processed/11_excel.result_sheet_All_Rotations.csv", header = TRUE)

excel.result.l <- excel.result %>% 
  pivot_longer(-c(var, stat), names_to = "WB", values_to = "Excel.value") %>%
  mutate(WB = sub("WB.", "WB ", WB)) %>%
  mutate(WB.var = paste(WB, var, sep = "_"))
excel.result.l.mean <- excel.result.l %>% 
  subset(stat == "mean")

r.excel <- excel.result.l.mean %>% select(-WB, -var, -stat) %>% 
  left_join(r.result.l, by = "WB.var") %>% select(-WB.var) %>%
  relocate(WB, 1) %>% relocate(Excel.value, .after = R.value) %>%
  subset(!is.na(WB)) %>%
  mutate(diff = Excel.value - R.value) %>%
  mutate(diff.pc = round(c(Excel.value - R.value)*100/Excel.value))

r.excel.diff <- r.excel %>%
  select(WB, var.excel, diff) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "WB", values_from = "diff")

write.csv(r.excel , file = "output/water_budgets/R_vs_Excel_water.budget.annual.climatology_mean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(r.excel.diff , file = "output/water_budgets/diff_R_from_Excel_annual.climatology_mean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### 4. Mean Monthly Perspective - Water Balance

```{r, mo-wb, fig.show = 'hold', fig.align='center', eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, fig.cap='Figure 5. Monthly climatalogy of water fluxes (median + 95 CI) for various cropping systems. Note that recharge is depicted in negative terms on the water consumption axis. Cropping systems are organised in order of increasing annual irrigation, followed by decreasing annual recharge.', include=TRUE}

# 1. Process data
clim.crop.cs <- process_monthly_climatology(budget, crop.systems)

# 2. Prepare for plotting (Ordering logic)
mo_plot_data <- clim.crop.cs %>%
  filter(var %in% c("plot.recharge", "plot.aet", "plot.etc", "plot.irri")) %>%
  mutate(var_f = fct_recode(var, "Potential Crop ET" = "plot.etc", "Actual ET" = "plot.aet", 
                            "-Recharge" = "plot.recharge", "Pumping" = "plot.irri"),
         var_f = factor(var_f, levels = c("Potential Crop ET",
                            "Actual ET", "-Recharge", "Pumping")))
# Add this logic before generating Figure 4
irri_order <- clim.crop.cs %>%
  filter(var == "plot.irri") %>%
  group_by(crop.system) %>%
  summarise(total_irri = sum(median, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(total_irri)

mo_plot_data$crop.system <- factor(mo_plot_data$crop.system, levels = irri_order$crop.system)

# 3. Plot Water Balance Terms
p.monthly.budget <- ggplot(mo_plot_data, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975, fill = var_f), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median, color = var_f), linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap( ~ crop.system) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12) +
  theme_baseR +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8)) +
  labs(y = "Water Consumption (mm)", title = "Monthly Water Use & Recharge")
print(p.monthly.budget)
ggsave(plot = p.monthly.budget, file = paste0("figures/water_budgets/04_monthly_climatology_water_budget_median.jpg"), width = 11.52 , height = 7.49)
```

Positive values are depicted in blue (Blue Water), negative values in red. Cropping systems are organised in decreasing order of annual Blue Water potential.', include=TRUE}

clim.crop.cs <- clim.crop.cs %>%

## 5. Archetype Village-Level Blue Water Potential 1950 Vs. 2022

```{r}

# 1. CONFIGURATION (Surgical control over typography and lane spacing)
cfg <- list(
  v_stagger_in   = 4400,   # Vertical spacing for left-side blue arrows
  v_stagger_out  = 4600,   # EXPANDED: Wider vertical spacing for right-side red arrows
  box_width      = 42,     
  arrow_head_sz  = 0.12,   
  min_arrow_w    = 1.5,    
  max_arrow_w    = 13,     
  text_sz_box    = 5.9,      # Enlarged central box text
  text_sz_main   = 4.2,    # Enlarged left-side labels
  text_sz_out    = 4.2,    # ENLARGED: Crisp, readable right-side labels
  text_sz_year   = 10,    
  tanker_vol_m3  = 10,     
  days_in_year   = 365,
  lpcd           = 100     
)

# 2. DATA INPUT
village <- readxl::read_xlsx("data/raw/Model in Excel/For Rutuja_BWP_Farm.xlsx", sheet = "BWP farm Fig 4 and 5")
village <- village %>%
  slice(-1) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(1, 2), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(1, 2), round))

village.bwp <- village %>% 
  select(`Time period`, `Social category of farm`, `BWP/farm...7`)

colnames(village.bwp) <- c("period", "label", "val")

data_list <- list(
  "1950" = subset(village.bwp, period == "1950s"),
  "2022" = subset(village.bwp, period == "2022")
)

display_labels <- list("1950" = "1950s", "2022" = "2022")

# 4. EXECUTE SYSTEM AND EXPORT
fig.6_journal <- get_village_comparison_plot(data_list, display_labels, cfg)
ggsave("figures/manuscript/Fig.6_Village Comparison_BWP.png", fig.6_journal, width = 17, height = 9.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# PRESENTATION VERSION
ggsave("figures/presentation/Fig.6_Village Comparison_BWP.png", fig.6_journal, width = 17, height = 9.5, dpi = 300, bg = "transparent")
print(fig.6_journal)
